items.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018
items.q: I mean I was working with a singer named Carrie Smith who my mother got me a job with, this was in the early 80s.

ctx.x: Right. Was that an odd experience? The first time you saw that?

Not odd. I mean it was great. I mean I was working with a singer named Carrie Smith who my mother got me a job with, this was in the early 80s. And she was a Gospel jazz singer who worked a lot in Europe, you know, worked a lot with big bands and different ensembles, traveled overseas quite a bit. So she wanted to replace one of the singers that was working with her. I think she must have known, she was from Newark — not from Newark but she had resided in Newark for a long time. So I think one of these singers…

Okay. I have a small story about that because I used to be in a band, basically a progressive rock band, and when my kids, we had some footage of it, and when we put it on for them, they didn’t want to watch it.
